rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation in tanh_activation_kernel_half (line 64). Fixed spec: dtype=float32. Dispatch: if(scalar_t==Half) uses half kernel, else uses vectorized kernel. float32 triggers vectorized kernel, so half kernel never executes. Mutated code path unreachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation affects only the half-precision kernel `tanh_activation_kernel_half`, but the fixed input specification mandates dtype=torch.float32. With float32 inputs, the AT_DISPATCH macro selects `tanh_activation_kernel_vectorized` instead of the half kernel. The mutated line 64 is in dead code for this configuration. Even auxiliary float16 testing cannot expose the bug because the thread launch parameters (designed for vec_size=4) only spawn 65,536 threads for 262,144 elements, so max idx=65,535 << size=262,144, making the boundary condition idx==size unreachable.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed contract. Requires dtype=torch.float16 AND a tensor size where total_threads >= size. The launch config bug (using vec_size=4 for half kernel thread count) compounds the issue.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of GPU kernels with dtype-specialized paths, ensure the fixed input specification covers ALL dtype branches that contain distinct logic. Alternatively, create separate test contracts per dtype. Also note the latent bug: the half kernel uses num_blocks calculated for vec_size=4 but processes 1 element per thread, causing under-coverage for large tensors.
